paragraphs: Friend, here's what I love about this song. David walks up to the LORD and asks Him to look at his life. Then he says, "Test me, O LORD, and try me; examine my heart and mind." (Psalm 26:2) That's a man who isn't hiding anything in the back of the pantry, and I know a little about people hiding things in the back of a drawer.

But listen to HOW he says it. David isn't bragging about a perfect record. His eyes are on something else: "Your loving devotion is before my eyes." (Psalm 26:3) The walking with integrity, the clean hands and the love for God's house all grow out of that. He's looking at God's faithful love, and that's what keeps his feet going the right way.

And watch where the song lands. He says he will walk with integrity, and in the very next breath he asks, "redeem me and be merciful to me." (Psalm 26:11) Then he finishes standing on level ground, ready to bless the LORD with God's people. (Psalm 26:12) So here's the big idea, baker: you can be honest about how you're walking, and you can still lean on God's mercy to hold you up. Walk straight, stay close to the LORD, and let His loving devotion be what you keep your eyes on.
